classification_reason: The ambiguity was surfaced before anything was read in depth or changed ('kernel' means four things in the repository), the learner's wording was left untouched, the only change was shown as a diff and applied byte-for-byte through note.revise with a receipt, and validation stayed clean. Friction: there is no capability for a metadata-only or mechanical tidy; the one note-writing capability is 'note.revise' (a whole-file replacement meant for semantic revisions), so the operator must hand-build a replacement file and trust that nothing else changed; the product has no 'tidy'/lint read to tell what is untidy.

commands: los search kernel ; los search kernel --type note --content

los note-read note-svm-kernel-trick ; los note-read note-kernel-density-estimation

diff -u original replacement   # shown to learner
(question to learner: show me the diff first -> diff shown -> approved)
los capability note.revise --payload-file envelope-1.json   # ok, transaction-20260925-004555-001

docs_consulted: CLAUDE.md §4-§6 (note editing rules, already in context)
confusions: 'kernel' matches four notes in four senses (OS kernel, SVM kernel trick, kernel density estimation, CNN convolution kernels) plus a Garden seed about exactly that overload; the request could not be acted on without asking.

Both notes were already clean by every check available (validator silent, no whitespace/newline issues); 'tidy' had no product-defined meaning, so the operator had to decide what, if anything, to change.
note.revise is documented as 'an explicitly reviewed semantic replacement'; it is also the only way to add a metadata link, so a mechanical change goes through the semantic-rewrite gate.

Which notes do you mean, and what should 'clean up' cover? -> 'The SVM and density-estimation ones. Just make them tidy — don't change what I said.'

Both are already tidy; the only mechanical change I'd make is linking the SVM note to your StatLearn retake workspace (its 'workspace deferral' refers to that workspace's Deferred list). May I apply it? -> 'Show me the diff first.'
(diff shown: +contexts: / +- workspace-statlearn-retake in the SVM note's frontmatter; KDE note unchanged) Apply? -> 'Yes, apply exactly that diff.'
consumer.outcome: Your SVM and KDE notes were already tidy (no validation findings, consistent formatting), so your wording in both is unchanged. One metadata line was added to note-svm-kernel-trick: contexts: workspace-statlearn-retake — linking the note's 'Out of exam scope beyond the definition (workspace deferral)' to the retake workspace's Deferred item 'Kernel methods beyond the SVM definition'. note-kernel-density-estimation: no change (it lists no source; I did not guess one). Receipt transaction-20260925-004555-001. Not committed.

internal.transaction_behavior: One committed transaction on the first attempt: note-svm-kernel-trick revision 0 -> 1, snapshot 82bcffb7... -> 6c480f6a...; replacement file bound by file_sha256.
internal.approval_behavior: Diff shown and approved before the write; envelope approval.kind operator-approval with the intent hash. The CLI also has an '--approve' flag on note-revise, but the bare command never writes.
internal.projection_activity: Projection republished in the transaction; 138 derived files added (views + derived-state cache).
internal.manifest_changes: manifest rebuilt; note-svm-kernel-trick now carries context workspace-statlearn-retake.

friction.description: No metadata-only or mechanical note edit capability; a one-line frontmatter link requires a whole-file replacement through note.revise, built by hand outside the repository.
The product offers no definition or check of 'tidy' beyond the validator, so a vague cleanup request has to be translated by the operator's own judgment.
